nodes.name: Ti foam oxidation
nodes.procedure: The oxidation process occurs by immersing the Ti foam (MTI-KOREA, EQ-TiF-1106, porosity: 40%, thickness: 0.6 mm) into H2O2 solution (Aldrich, 50 wt%) at 70°C for 30 min.
nodes.source_text: Initially, the oxidation process occurs by immersing the Ti foam... into H2O2 solution... at 70°C for 30 min.

nodes.name: Mo-doping hydrothermal
nodes.procedure: Mo-doping of [oxidized] Ti foam is carried out through a hydrothermal method at 180°C for 12 h (at a heating rate of 10°C min⁻¹), utilizing a solution of 0.5 mmol MoCl5 (Aldrich, 99.99%) and 0.5 mmol TiCl4 (Aldrich, >99.0%) in 50 mL deionized water.
nodes.source_text: Subsequently, Mo-doping of Ti foam is carried out through a hydrothermal method at 180°C for 12 h (at a heating rate of 10°C min⁻¹), utilizing a solution of 0.5 mmol MoCl5... and 0.5 mmol TiCl4...

nodes.name: RuO2 NCs hydrothermal deposition
nodes.procedure: After overnight drying in a vacuum oven at 70°C, the deposition of Ru-based NCs is carried out hydrothermally using a 1 mmol RuCl3·xH2O (Aldrich, 99.98%) solution [in 50 mL deionized water] at 150°C for 10 h.

unit_operations.procedure_snippet: the deposition of Ru-based NCs is carried out hydrothermally using a 1 mmol RuCl3·xH2O solution at 150°C for 10 h

nodes.source_text: After overnight drying in a vacuum oven at 70°C, the deposition of Ru-based NCs is carried out hydrothermally using a 1 mmol RuCl3·xH2O solution at 150°C for 10 h.

nodes.name: Low-temperature annealing
nodes.procedure: Finally, the synthesized catalysts are annealed at a low temperature of 200°C, with varying annealing times of 0, 20, 40, and 60 min. Each sample is denoted as CS-Ru-0, 20, 40, and 60.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ti 2p3/2 (Ti4+) at 458.0 eV and Ru 3p3/2 (Ru4+) at 462.7 eV pre-HER; post-HER shows increased Ru0 at 461.1 eV, decreased Ti4+ peak shifting to lower binding energy indicating reduction to porous TiOx shell. Mo 3d shows increased Mo0 peak post-HER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS spectra of the core-level Ti 2p and Ru 3p (Fig. S15, ESI†) show the Ti 2p3/2 peak (Ti4+ at 458.0 eV) and Ru 3p3/2 peak (Ru4+ at 462.7 eV) ... the RuO2 core NCs are significantly reduced to metallic Ru during the electrochemical reduction (Fig. 3c), with the intensity of the Ru0 peak at 461.1 eV increasing after 50 HER cycles ... the Ti4+ peak of the pre-HER sample also decreases and shifts towards lower binding energy after HER, indicating partial dissolution and reduction of Ti4+ ions to form a porous TiOx shell. ... Mo 3d XPS profile also shows an increase in the Mo0 peak

nodes.characterization_summary: EELS spectrum shows Ti L-edge signals partially observed from certain areas of NC surface with varying intensities, corroborating existence of porous titania shell.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EELS spectrum obtained at different locations on a single CS-Ru-40 NC ... Ti L-edge signals are partially observed from certain areas of the NC surface, and their intensities are also different depending on the location, corroborating the existence of a porous titania shell.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS line-scan profiles confirm core–shell structure preserved after HER with Ru-based core, Ti-based shell, interfacial Mo atoms; atomic percentages Ti:Ru:Mo = 31.5:64.2:4.3 at%, Ti-to-Ru ratio decreases from 0.70 to 0.50 after HER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS line-scan profiles of metal elements measured from five different vertical positions ... atomic percentages of Ti, Ru, and Mo measured using EDS are 31.5, 64.2, and 4.3 at%, respectively, showing that the Ti-to-Ru ratio decreases from 0.70 to 0.50 after HER.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pore-size distribution analysis confirms presence of subnanometer-sized pores (0.55 nm).
nodes.evidence_snippet: presence of the subnanometer-sized pores (0.55 nm) was confirmed from the pore-size distribution analysis using the gas adsorption method

nodes.evidence_snippet: high mass activity of 2.18 A mg^-1, calculated based on the small amount of Ru (0.16 mg_Ru cm^-2) obtained by inductively coupled plasma-mass spectroscopy (ICP-MS ...
